messages:
mira (sec-eng): Quick question — during a failover drill we saw services in us-west-2 fail to decrypt envelope data keys that were generated against our MRK primary in us-east-1. We used GenerateDataKey, stored the ciphertextDataKey with the object. When we simulated us-east-1 being unreachable, Decrypt in us-west-2 returned AccessDenied on the ciphertext blob. Anyone seen this behavior?

devon (infra): Do you mean you used a multi-Region key (MRK) with a replica in us-west-2 or a separate single-region CMK? Grants or key policy could matter here.

mira (sec-eng): It was an MRK primary in us-east-1 + a replica in us-west-2. The app in us-west-2 uses the replica's ARN for KMS calls post-failover. We originally created cross-account grants in us-east-1 for the service role in the other account.

alice (cloud-sec): That explains it — grants are regional and bound to the specific CMK in that region. Grants you created in us-east-1 are not visible on the replica key in us-west-2. In failover the replica needs its own grants or a key policy that allows the principal. TL;DR: don't rely only on grants for cross-region failover.

sam (platform): Also check the ciphertext metadata. MRK ciphertext blobs include info tying them to the multi-Region key. A proper MRK replica *can* decrypt a ciphertext created by any replica/primary of the same MRK, but only if the replica is configured and the principal has permission on that replica. If permissions are missing you'll get AccessDenied, not a network error.

mira (sec-eng): Good to know. So options are: (1) provision identical grants in every replica region via automation (terraform/CFN), (2) prefer key policy + IAM role so permissions exist across replicas, or (3) rewrap data keys in the failover region (ugh).

alice (cloud-sec): Yep. Key policy is the most robust for DR because it survives region failover. Example minimal policy fragment to allow an external account role to use the key (adapt ARNs):

```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "AllowExternalServiceRole",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::555666777888:role/ci-service-role"},
      "Action": ["kms:Decrypt", "kms:GenerateDataKey*", "kms:DescribeKey"],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```

alice (cloud-sec): That policy needs to be applied to each replica CMK key policy (or to the primary and have the replicas inherit in MRK config depending on how you provision). We usually keep identical key policy documents across regions for MRKs.

devon (infra): Note: grants are also useful for temporary, least-privilege access (they can be created by the principal that needs them), but since they are not replicated, add a bootstrap step in your failover playbook to recreate necessary grants in the replica region before promoting it.

sam (platform): Another gotcha — if your service assumes a cross-account role and then calls KMS, make sure the role is explicitly in the key policy or has an effective policy via IAM. Also check for use of GrantToken in the client if you create grants programmatically during the same request sequence.

mira (sec-eng): Understood. Action items for us: (A) add IaC to create matching grants/key-policy entries in all replica regions, (B) update DR runbook to recreate grants if needed, (C) run an end-to-end test where data key is generated in primary and decrypted in replica while primary is unreachable. Anyone want to volunteer to own automation (A)?

ops-bot: Reminder: tag incident playbook "kms-mrk-failover" for postmortem and invite runbook authors. :white_check_mark:

devon (infra): I'll take automation (A). I'll prototype terraform that ensures the same key policy + grants are applied to replica CMKs. I'll also add a small test that calls GenerateDataKey in us-east-1 and then Decrypt in us-west-2 with the replica principal.

alice (cloud-sec): Thanks. One last note on rotation: if you enable automatic rotation on MRKs, rotation of key material happens per-region; make sure your automation handles any rotation sanity checks and that replicas remain in sync for policy/grants.

mira (sec-eng): Great — thanks everyone. I'll update the playbook and schedule a follow-up test next week. :thumbsup:
